name: Caldera Springs
label: Caldera Springs
about_prose: Caldera Springs sits fifteen miles south of Bend, next to Sunriver Resort, at roughly 4,170 feet of elevation in the high desert along the upper Deschutes River. The community's own design guidelines place the site in a semi-arid Montane Life Zone, a transition band between the Great Basin Desert and the Cascade Range, covered in ponderosa and lodgepole pine with an understory of sagebrush, bitterbrush, and manzanita. Average annual precipitation runs 18 inches and average snowfall 49 inches, though the range swings hard from year to year. One winter brought 13 inches of snow, the next brought 144, according to those same guidelines. Every builder in the community designs around that swing. Snow-load framing, solar gain through winter windows, and wildfire resistance all run through the same approval process. Caldera Springs holds Firewise Community status, and the guidelines require wildfire-resistant roofing, building materials, and defensible landscaping before anyone breaks ground.

PacTrust opened the community in 2006 on 400 acres, with an original plan for 320 single-family homesites and 45 cabins. A 600-acre eastward expansion, launched in 2021, brought the master plan to its current 1,000 acres. Roughly a fifth of that total, 220 acres, was set aside rather than built on, carried in the plat as a protected wildlife mitigation area and marketed today as the Wildlife Forest Preserve. The lake and stream system at the center of the community, 14.7 acres of water including Obsidian Lake and Trailmere Lake, predates the expansion and still anchors it. So does Caldera Links, a nine-hole, par-27 course designed by golf architect Bob Cupp, with holes running a tight 60 to 185 yards and built for an afternoon rather than a full day on the course.

The most recent capital investment landed in 2024. Forest House added a family aquatics complex with a dual-racer water slide and a 1,748-square-foot fitness center. Forest Park added six pickleball courts, a dog park, and a winter sledding hill. The Lake House reopened on Obsidian Lake as Sunriver Resort's eleventh restaurant, open to the public and not just to owners. Thirteen miles of paved and soft-surface trail tie the lakes to the forest, and The Outpost rents kayaks, canoes, and paddleboards for the water. Owners also get access to the Spa at Sunriver Resort, a reminder that Caldera Springs is managed in connection with the resort next door, under Sunriver Resort's operator, CoralTree Hospitality, and not as a fully separate community.

Three kinds of homes exist here. Custom single-family residences are built lot by lot to the community's own standards. Caldera Cabins are the smaller product from the original 2006 plan. Forestbrook is the newest, three- and four-bedroom homes with attached studios, floor-to-ceiling windows, and private hot tubs, built to enter Sunriver Resort's vacation-rental program when an owner is away. The first Forestbrook homes were delivered in the summer of 2024. Every home, cabin or custom build, goes through the Caldera Springs Owners' Association's Design Review Committee. The guidelines do not mandate one architectural style, but they steer new construction toward what they call Northwest Mountain style, a family of Cascadian, Lodge, Ranch, Craftsman, and Northwest Contemporary forms. They also set a 30-foot maximum building height and a 1,600-square-foot minimum on habitable space for anything other than a cabin or cottage. The CSOA, the homeowners' association behind that review process, is a separate body from Sunriver Resort's own management.

Kids in the community feed into Three Rivers School, a K-8 public school in Sunriver and one of 36 schools in the Bend-La Pine School District. That K-8 structure matters before you buy. There is no town center inside the gates and no high school on site, so daily life runs on a drive, into Sunriver Village for basics or up US-97 into Bend for anything larger. The other trade-off is that privacy only goes so far here. The golf course, the trails, and now the Lake House restaurant are shared with Sunriver Resort's overnight guests as well as owners, so a quiet Tuesday morning at Obsidian Lake can turn crowded the moment resort occupancy fills for a holiday weekend. And every custom home has to clear the Design Review Committee before a shovel goes in the ground, which protects the look of the neighborhood but limits how far a buyer can depart from the approved Northwest Mountain palette.

amenities.name: Lake House
amenities.description: Waterfront restaurant on Obsidian Lake with indoor-outdoor dining and Mt. Bachelor views, plus the adjacent Shore Shack walkup bar with fire-pit seating.

amenities.name: Forest House
amenities.description: Recreation center with multiple heated outdoor pools, one of Oregon's longest dual-racer water slides, a lazy river, a kids' pool, a 1,748-square-foot fitness center, a game room, and poolside dining.
amenities.access: Owners and Sunriver Resort vacation-home guests only

amenities.name: The Quarry
amenities.description: Infinity-edge pool overlooking Obsidian Lake, outdoor year-round spas, and a fitness center with stocked locker rooms.

amenities.name: Forest Park
amenities.description: Four-season park with six pickleball courts, a dog park, a children's play area, and a winter sledding hill.

amenities.name: Caldera Links Golf Course
amenities.description: A 9-hole, par-27 course designed by Bob Cupp, with holes from 60 to 185 yards plus putting and chipping greens.

amenities.name: Lakes and Trails
amenities.description: 14.7 acres of lakes and streams with paddleboard, kayak, and canoe rentals through The Outpost, connected by 13 miles of paved and soft trails.

amenities.name: Spa at Sunriver Resort
amenities.description: Full-service spa at the adjacent Sunriver Resort, with complimentary fitness-center access for Caldera Springs owners and guests.

amenities.name: Wildlife Forest Preserve
amenities.description: A 220-acre permanently protected open space supporting habitat for river otters and bald eagles observed on the community's waterways.
